subject: Proof of non-learning & EU residency — evidence pack and runbook
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clinicalview.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Bates <simon.bates@clinicalview.com>, ClinicalView Legal <legal@clinicalview.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: proof-of-non-learning + EU residency details

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal has come back with two gating asks before procurement can move forward: 1) a concise evidence pack that demonstrates Redwood does not use Customer prompts/responses to train models (or the technical controls that prevent it); and 2) confirmation and supporting artifacts that customer traffic for ClinicalView customer IDs can be processed and stored in EU-only infrastructure (KMS in EU, onshore processing, and a subprocessor list scoped to EU residency).

Can you share:
- a one-page runbook / checklist we can hand to our legal & security team showing what artifacts you will provide (logs, on-demand exports, SFTP examples, audit trail queries), and
- a rough timeline for delivery (we need something for legal review by the end of next week).

Attachments: ClinicalView_Risk_Assessment.docx (provided by ClinicalView)

Appreciate a quick outline we can include in the procurement packet.

Best,
Maya

--
Maya Patel
Head of IT Procurement, ClinicalView
maya.patel@clinicalview.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clinicalview.com>, Simon Bates <simon.bates@clinicalview.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: proof-of-non-learning + EU residency details

Team — forwarding ClinicalView's ask. They need a short, consumer-friendly evidence pack plus the ops runbook for handoff to their legal/security. Legal wants artifacts that prove: no model training on their prompts, EU residency for processing and keys, and a scoped subprocessor inventory limited to EU operations (or clear routing for non-EU subprocessors).

Initial proposed deliverables (draft):
- "Non-learning Runbook (one-pager)" — short steps and toggles we use (learning toggle, ephemeral KV policy, redaction rules).
- "Evidence pack (zip)" — sample audit queries (time-window), sample SFTP export manifest, example KMS key ID showing EU region, and a sanitized log snippet showing no model-updates triggered by tenant traffic.
- "Subprocessor inventory (CSV)" — filtered to subprocessors involved in EU processing + contractual residency notes.
- Timeline: draft runbook + inventory by EOD Thursday; evidence pack (sample artifacts) by next Tuesday.

Questions:
1) David — can ops produce a sanitized log snippet + a sample KMS key export by Thu?
2) Kimberly — legal needs a crisp one-line statement we can include in the runbook about derivative ownership/tenant output licensing. Can you propose wording?
3) Neha — are there any known non-EU subprocessors that will still touch ClinicalView data in a way we need to disclose (e.g., monitoring, billing)? If so, note routing & fallback.

I'll draft the runbook outline and share a template. Attaching the outline I promised.

Attachments: nonlearning_runbook_outline.pdf

Thanks — Evelyn

--
Evelyn Hart
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Evelyn / team — quick technical confirmation and what I can deliver by Thu: 

What we can produce by Thursday EOD (sanitized/demo-ready):
- Sanitized audit log snippet showing request IDs, tenant ID, and absence of any training-job triggers or model snapshot events for the window. (ops-proof-template.csv attached)
- KMS key metadata export that highlights key region (eu-west-1) and key policy (note: we will redact account IDs for the demo but provide full values in the secure evidence transfer).
- SFTP export manifest sample showing a daily export package (file list) with checksums — shows how a tenant export can be performed.
- Short note on how the learning toggle works (disabled for ClinicalView by default on their tenant) and how ephemeral KV is retained for 24hrs then purged.

Technical caveats / asks:
- For a full proof pack (not sanitized), we need a signed NDA/secure SFTP share (they already have procurement, so we'll request a signed evidence access form).
- We also need confirmation from Neha on whether billing/metrics pipes touch any US-based telemetry pipelines that we should include in the subprocessor list.

Attachment: ops-proof-template.csv

Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T16:03:00Z
Subject: Non-learning evidence pack & runbook (draft) — ClinicalView

Hi Maya / Simon / ClinicalView Legal —

Attached is a draft evidence pack and a concise runbook intended for legal/security review. High-level summary below and next steps: 

What we included (attached zip):
- nonlearning_runbook_draft.pdf — one-page runbook that explains learning toggle, ephemeral KV retention (24h), model variant routing, and how we isolate tenant data during inference.
- cv_nonlearning_checklist.xlsx — checklist matching the runbook items to artifacts we can provide on request.
- ops-proof-template.csv — sanitized sample logs & SFTP manifest showing the export path and checksums.
- kms_key_rotation_policy.pdf — metadata showing EU key id (eu-west-1) and rotation policy (sanitized).

Short answers to your two asks:
1) Proof we do not train on customer data: we apply a per-tenant learning toggle and do not include tenant traffic in model improvement pipelines without explicit opt-in. The attached sanitized logs and the runbook explain how to verify this (audit query examples included). For full forensic proof, we can produce the non-sanitized artifacts via secure SFTP under an evidence-access agreement.
2) EU-only processing & keys: ClinicalView tenant data can be pinned to EU processing nodes and EU KMS keys. The attached KMS metadata shows EU key IDs; subprocessor inventory (included in the spreadsheet) lists subprocessors that act on EU data.

Open items for procurement/legal acceptance:
- Kimberly: proposed single-sentence statement on derivative rights for the runbook: "Tenant outputs are licensed to the tenant; Redwood does not claim ownership of tenant-generated prompts or outputs and will not use them to train models unless explicitly contracted." Can you confirm or redline?
- Neha: confirm whether telemetry/billing signals that flow to third-party monitoring are within EU or require disclosure.

Next steps: if this looks good, we'll package the full (non-sanitized) evidence in a secure transfer once ClinicalView signs the evidence access form (I can send it). Looking to close legal review by next Wed.

Attachments: nonlearning_runbook_draft.pdf, cv_nonlearning_checklist.xlsx, ops-proof-template.csv, kms_key_rotation_policy.pdf

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Phone: +1-415-555-0142

--
Evelyn H.
